messages.author: 234b19e16acd8f48
messages.subject: How to use attributes in other functions
parts:
Dear all,

Inside a trajectory I am setting an attribute to the current time. Then I would like to pass this time to a function file so that it can calculate specific things. However when I try to do this in the following way, it handles it as an function and not as a variable. How can I change this so that I can work with the attributes as variables (that are different for each trajectory)?

env <- simmer()

patient <-
  trajectory("patient's path") %>%
  log_("Here I am") %>%
  set_attribute("start_time", function() {now(env)}) %>% 
  next_function(function() {get_attribute(env, "start_time")})

next_function <- function(traj, time){
  if(time < 5){
     log_(traj, "small time"){
  else{
    log_(traj, "big time")
  }
 return(traj)
}
 
now it gives the error that it cannot compare time with a integer, because it is a function.. However when I remove the function inside the next_function() it gives the error no arrival happening.

Thank you in advance,
Greetings Wessel

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] How to use attributes in other functions
parts:
Hi Wessel,
I restructured your code a bit, have a look at it. Is this what you are trying to achieve?

Best,
Bart


library(simmer)

env <- simmer()

my_function <- function(attrs){
  time <- attrs['start_time']
  if(time < 5){
    print("small time")
  } else{
    print("big time")
  }
  
  return(0) # timeout will be of duration 0

}

patient <-
  trajectory("patient's path") %>%
  log_("Here I am") %>%
  set_attribute("start_time", function() {now(env)}) %>%

timeout(my_function)


env %>%
  add_generator("patient", patient, at(seq(0,10,1))) %>%
  run()

Note that the old method for retrieving attributes as an argument is
deprecated. This function should be rewritten as follows:

my_function <- function(){
time <- get_attribute(env, 'start_time')

if(time < 5){
print("small time")
} else{
print("big time")
}
return(0) # timeout will be of duration 0
}

I'm not sure I understand what exactly you want to accomplish, but:

If you need to follow different sub-trajectories based on certain
conditions, then you need the branch() activity. You'll find several
examples in the vignettes. If you need one path, without forks, but
you want modularity and reuse, you can define parts of the trajectory
and then concatenate them with join(). If you want to stop at some
point (for instance, run path1 but not path2 if some condition holds),
you need to place the leave() activity between path1 and path2.

Iñaki

parts:
2017-09-18 9:54 GMT+02:00 Wessel de Zeeuw <wessel...@gmail.com>:
> I am sorry for my bad explanation.
>
> What I mean is the following:
> I have a trajectory which calls a function my_function. In that function it
> checks what the time is. If the time is small we want the trajectory to do
> specific things (so wait, branch or join a different traj) and when the time
> is big it does something different. So that would do something like this:
>
> my_function <- function(){
> time <- get_attribute(env, start_time)
> if(time < 5){
> return(time) #we want the trajectory to wait small time
> } else{
> join(t1) #join a new trajectory
> return(0)
> }

simmer's golden rule: one activity, one action; and vice versa. You
cannot wait some time OR follow another path in the same activity. You
have to break down your actions and put them into different
activities. For example:

my_function <- function(){
time <- get_attribute(env, start_time)
if(time < 5){

return(1) # we want the trajectory to wait small time
} else{
return(2) # we want to join a new trajectory
}

my_trajectory <- trajectory() %>%
...
branch(my_function, continue=c(T, F), # or whatever
# option 1
timeout(function() get_attribute(env, "start_time")),
# option 2
